listen.script: Many people think energy drinks help you study. However, doctors warn that the high levels of caffeine can disturb your sleep. According to recent research, students who sleep well actually remember more, so water and an early night are a better choice before an exam.
listen.q: What does the speaker recommend before an exam?
options: An energy drink and late revision

listen.script: The person I'd like to talk about is my aunt, who's a nurse. She works night shifts, which meant that she often missed family dinners. Having said that, she always found time to help me with my science homework, and that's why I want to work in medicine.
listen.q: Why does the speaker want to work in medicine?

read.passage: Saudi Arabia produces more desalinated water than any other country, and much of the drinking water in its cities comes from the sea. Desalination, however, uses a great deal of energy, so experts urge people to treat water as a valuable resource. It is estimated that a dripping tap can waste thousands of litres a year, yet many families never think about such small leaks. Some people argue that one household saving water is just a drop in the ocean. Researchers point out, though, that small changes add up when millions of people make them. Shorter showers, fixing leaks and running the washing machine only when it is full are simple steps. Newer desalination plants are also using solar power, which could make the process cleaner in the future.

qs.q: Why do experts want people to save water?
options: Because desalination uses a lot of energy
Because there is no sea nearby

qs.q: What do some people argue about one household saving water?

options: Small changes add up across millions of people.
